note: Destination evidence updated 2026-10-02 after real PostgreSQL and live browser verification, and extended with the contract-contribution port. PARTIAL means tested implementation exists but the full preservation criterion is not met; task handoffs bound each claim.

C01.evidence: Entra signature/tenant/audience/scope validation; membership plus an explicit scoped RoleGrant is now required, with expiry, recorded revocation and firm/client/engagement scope enforced in the guard and reapplied inside each write transaction. Not implemented: session/access epoch revocation, segregation-of-duties combinations and a grant administration surface.

C02.evidence: No tenant consent, capability verification or directory provisioning service exists in the destination.

C03.evidence: Per-client repository bindings resolved per purpose (evidence/working), immutable provider-version identity recorded in DocumentVersion, and reads served from the version endpoint with eTag and SHA-256 verification; production fails closed without a binding. Not implemented: site provisioning, tenant consent, live permission verification and retention controls.

C05.evidence: Pure fee model ported from the source: sum(hours × rate) → complexity → risk premium → discount with every stage rounded to two decimals half-to-even so the breakdown reconciles to the fee, plus input validation that fails closed and a canonical input hash. The configurable approval matrix is ported with its fail-safe Partner default. docs/migration/03-differential-report.md reports 46/46 checks matched. Not implemented: persisted quotation versions, tender/proposal documents, dispatch and client acceptance of an exact version.

C06.evidence: Real dual-key gate: Key 1 (accepted proposal with client evidence) and Key 2 (RISK_PARTNER_CLEAR clearance with reason) are persisted records; ISSUE_ENGAGEMENT_LETTER refuses either missing key and issues an immutable ISA 210 letter pinning the exact revision and fee. Not implemented: the full ISA 220 questionnaire tracks, continuance path and acceptance cases.

C07.evidence: Canonical firm-numbered engagement invoices (ADVANCE_50/FINAL_50) with immutable payments and one receipt per settled invoice; the advance chain gates portal activation (INV-002). Not implemented: ledger posting of invoices, credit notes, AR aging, and fee agreement documents.

C08.evidence: Client portal is a disabled layout with no client identity/session contract.

C10.evidence: No client accounting profiles/periods/books; target Engagement is a flat scalar record.

C11.evidence: Bounded CSV upload to staging with sha256 duplicate detection, PG outbox, BullMQ parsing, transactional set-based mapping and zero-sum finalization. Monetary columns are numeric(28,6) with a six-decimal contract. A finalized import now publishes an immutable accepted balance version bound to that exact import version, with capability, state, completeness and zero-sum checks. Concurrent identical uploads now coalesce into one authoritative import, every stored object is tracked before its bytes exist, and a grace-period sweep removes only unreferenced objects while durable Graph evidence is reported for review. Not implemented: XLSX, multi-period/entity intake, sealed source acceptance and currency-aware publication.

C12.evidence: No general-ledger import or completeness checks.

C13.evidence: Optimistic per-row versions, idempotency receipts and engagement-row locking, plus firm-scoped versioned taxonomies whose approved versions and lines are immutable by database trigger, and a mapping approval that binds one import's mapped rows to an exact taxonomy version by digest. Any later row change makes the approval stale, and publication now requires a current approval. Approved mappings build client-scoped memory with the approval as provenance, and a read-only suggestion endpoint offers remembered codes (reporting unknown accounts, retired codes and already-mapped rows explicitly). A staff workspace now authors taxonomy versions through the guarded endpoint with repeating validated lines, approves draft versions, binds an import's mapping approval to the exact approved version, and reviews per-import suggestions read-only with named reasons and approval provenance. Not implemented: allocations, statement layouts/financial packages, and a corrections workflow.

C14.evidence: No statement drill-down or currency review query.

C15.evidence: Client audit adjustment journals kept separate from the firm's own ledger: balanced double-entry drafts, posting under a distinct capability with a preparer/poster separation of duties, database-enforced balance and at-least-two-lines at posting, and a posted journal frozen except for one transition to REVERSED via a reversal journal that swaps the sides. The workspace now authors more than two lines through a shared repeating editor with per-line six-decimal validation and a submission gate that refuses incomplete lines, and derived adjusted balances are exposed over the latest publication plus posted journals. Not implemented: adjustment plans, persisted adjusted-balance snapshots, eligibility queries and the differences register.

C22.evidence: Pure calculator ported from the source with identical arithmetic: benchmark derivation from mapped sections with tax excluded from profit before tax, per-benchmark policy validation, PM/TE/SAD on a decimal-safe six-decimal primitive, risk bands with minimum owner rank, and an input hash. docs/migration/03-differential-report.md reports 14/14 checks matched against source-quoted fixtures. Assessments are now persisted against an exact published balance version and taxonomy version, require MATERIALITY_MANAGE to calculate and MATERIALITY_APPROVE to approve, forbid self-approval, become stale when a newer publication exists, and are frozen once approved. Risk is now persisted too: an append-only band-assessment series with the colour derived by the database from the recorded scores (a stored band that does not follow from its inputs is rejected), and mandatory Partner clearance (`RISK_PARTNER_CLEAR`) of the current red band. Risk owners are assigned against the current assessment with a minimum staffing rank enforced both in the service and by a database trigger, red bands require prior Partner clearance, and a user cannot assign a risk to themselves. The `START_FIELDWORK` lifecycle command now refuses to start from an unapproved or stale plan. Not implemented: routing risks into workprograms, the risk/planning UI, and the same staleness gate for later lifecycle steps.

C23.evidence: No audit planning or program library.

C24.evidence: No fieldwork schedules, item tests or area assessments.

C25.evidence: Deterministic engine ported from the source with the same fixed splitmix64 generator: MUS interval crossing, key-item threshold, seeded random draw, stratified key-item-plus-draw, zero-exposure exclusion, absolute-exposure selection with signed totals and a six-decimal coverage percentage. docs/migration/03-differential-report.md reports 33/33 checks matched overall. Not implemented: persisted immutable populations and execution records, physical evidence movements and procedure conclusions.

C26.evidence: Anchored review notes with grant-based authority: REVIEW_RAISE to raise, REVIEW_RESOLVE to resolve, the raiser can never resolve their own note, one OPEN→RESOLVED transition, and a resolved note is frozen by trigger while notes are never deleted; the database independently rejects a self-resolved or inconsistently shaped row. Not implemented: reviewer inbox, rework loop, revision-aware anchoring, SRM compilation and manager/Partner clearances.

C29.evidence: No freeze/deadline/legal hold. The only immutability is DB triggers on finalized TB rows and audit events.

C30.evidence: Transactionally ordered audit sidecars, canonical event format, SHA-256 predecessor chain, independent checkpoint manifest interface and scoped verifier. Concurrent writes, rollback and tampering are tested against PostgreSQL. Audit writes now carry actor kind, resource identity, correlation and redacted before/after payloads with database-enforced traceability; service actors need no synthetic user id; application credentials hold no UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE on audit rows; authorization denials are appended to a separate append-only SecurityEvent log that survives transaction rollback, and a scoped history read rechecks ENGAGEMENT_READ server-side. Not implemented: the canonical digest does not yet cover the new metadata columns, call sites still write plain USER events, and no immutable archive bundle, live signed checkpoint storage, retention assurance or release checkpoint exists.

C32.evidence: Firm-wide authorized chart, active/posting accounts, non-overlapping date-only periods, policy-gated balanced journal posting, immutable posted headers and lines, exact append-only reversing journals, trial balance query and Practice UI. PostgreSQL scope, balance, lock and race guards are implemented. Not implemented: invoices, payment allocations, credit notes, period reopening, bank reconciliation, monthly P/L and AR aging; full source parity remains incomplete.

C33.evidence: Contract contribution ported from ContractContributionCalculator.cs as a pure calculator: lifetime approved minutes valued at their captured charge-out rate, netted against the contracted fee, summed as an exact rational and rounded once half-to-even to six decimals. Missing rates, foreign currencies and negative inputs return unavailable rather than zero, and the metric is named fee-less-standard-value so it is never presented as payroll-cost profit (D07). docs/migration/03-differential-report.md reports 53/53 checks matched including 7 new contract-contribution checks quoted from ContractContributionCalculatorTests.cs. Not implemented: the PracticeAnalyticsQuery aggregation (engagement economics, department utilization, milestone performance), rate cards, timesheets, budgets and any API or UI.

C36.evidence: PostgreSQL outbox plus a reconciliation loop that republishes missing BullMQ jobs, with terminal-success handling and status fencing. Covers only the tb.import job family; no other operation types, no cancellation dispositions, no stale-worker fencing token.

C37.evidence: Upload/mapping/finalize contracts validated by Zod at the HTTP boundary and an internal guard. No no-store download policy, draft handling or equivalent non-TB journeys.

C38.evidence: Ten reviewed SQL migrations: append-only audit and lifecycle history, finalized-row and published-balance immutability, six-decimal monetary precision, compound firm/client/engagement scope foreign keys and grant scope/revocation/window check constraints. Check constraints, triggers, indexes and immutable-history coverage are still far short of the source's 252 tables.
